review_notes:
I read the whole file. I also read the torus helper definitions in Infra/Torus/Basic.lean (periodicToTorus, fromUnitTorus, toUnitTorus, unitTorusRepresentative and the round-trip lemmas). I read frozenInitialData_memLp_torus and the ScalarTorusL2 abbreviation, and I searched the Torus directory for existing bundled maps (LinearIsometry, continuous linear maps, equivalences) and found none.

The candidates I considered do not justify a bundling finding:
- scalarTorusRepresentative: it picks a pointwise representative of an Lp class, `fun x => f x`. That is not additive or linear, because Lp.coeFn_add holds only almost everywhere. Its only preserved quantities are periodicity and the L² norm, so a LinearMap, LinearIsometry or equivalence would be wrong or would need quotienting by a.e. equality.
- weakPathRepresentative: it is a time-indexed family of such representatives, zero outside [0,1]. Its lemmas are pointwise-in-time facts that are used as stated, not a homomorphism, equivalence or action.
- smoothPeriodicTestL2: it does map into Lp as a class, and that map is linear on the smooth periodic functions. But the domain is a pair of hypotheses (`hψ`, `_hperiodic`) on a bare function, not a bundled submodule. Building such a submodule and a LinearMap would add proof obligations, and I found no use in the file or in the related files I read that needs linearity or LinearMap API.
- The proofs of weakPathRepresentative_pairing_eq_inner and FrozenDriftProblem.initial_pairing_eq_cell_integral repeat one chain: unit-cell integral, torus integral, L2.inner_def. That duplication could be factored into a shared lemma, but it is not a failure to expose standard mathematical structure, so it is outside this rubric.

I did not search the whole repository exhaustively for consumers outside the FourierGalerkin directory, so a consumer that needs a bundled map could exist there.
